q: Total number of erstwhile Demands in Indian Railways (prior to merger - including both Revenue and Capital)
e: The correct answer is 16. Prior to the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget, Indian Railways presented 16 Demands for Grants — 15 revenue demands and a single works demand, Demand No. 16, covering all works expenditure irrespective of the source of financing. On the revenue side, Demands 3 to 13 formed Ordinary Working Expenses and Demands 1 to 15 together formed Gross Working Expenses. q: Which fund is described as "Reservoir of Government Money" ?
e: The correct answer is (C) the Consolidated Fund of India. Under Article 266(1) of the Constitution, all revenues received, loans raised and receipts by way of recovery of loans form the Consolidated Fund of India — it is the "reservoir of government money". Appropriation is Parliament's authorisation, through the Appropriation Act, to withdraw money from the Consolidated Fund for the voted demands.

q: Recovery of Provident Fund is accounted in ?
e: The correct answer is Public Account of India. Provident Fund subscriptions, recoveries and withdrawals are not government revenue, so under Article 266(2) of the Constitution they are accounted in the Public Account of India, where the government holds money in trust, as a banker. This is why PF, deposits and remittances never appear in the Consolidated Fund. Exam tip: anything the government holds in trust or as a liability goes to the Public Account.

q: Pick out the odd man out

q: Budget is a ________________ and _______________ document as per Indian Railway Finance Code Volume One (Chapter 3)
e: Option A (Constitutional , Management) is the correct choice. Under Chapter 3 of the Indian Railway Finance Code Volume I, the Budget is described as both a constitutional document — because Article 112 mandates the Annual Financial Statement and Parliament's sanction — and a management document, since it is the instrument through which the Railway Board plans, controls and reviews railway finances. q: As per Article 112(1) of Constitution of India, A statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for that year’ referred to as the "__________________________" and popularly called the "__________________".
e: annual financial statement, Annual Budget — that is the right answer. Article 112(1) requires the President to lay before Parliament a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for that financial year. Article 113 then deals with the procedure for Demands for Grants — estimates of expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund are shown separately from other, voted expenditure. q: The erstwhile Demands No. 1, 2 & 3 are in the nature of _______________
e: The correct answer is General on cost. These demands carry the common, overhead expenditure of the railway — Railway Board, miscellaneous general expenditure and general superintendence — which cannot be attributed to any single working-expense activity and is therefore treated as general on cost. q: There is a single works erstwhile Demand No. 16 for all works Expenditure irrespective of source of financing. Say True or False

q: Accounts Dept (PFA) responsibility towards Budget is _______
e: The correct answer is Compilation and scrutiny. The spending departments (the executives) prepare the estimates, but the Accounts Department under the Principal Financial Adviser compiles them into the budget and scrutinises them for correctness, classification and adequacy of provision. The PFA neither prepares the raw estimates nor approves the budget — approval rests with the Railway Board and Parliament. Notice how precisely the correct option is worded. Voted expenditure requires Parliament's approval through demands for grants; it can be reduced or rejected during voting.
